precepts.text: God had sworn to David that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne; according to the flesh, not the spirit.
precepts.point: In Isaiah 7 Ahaz would not ask a sign, so the Lord gave one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, and before the child knew to refuse the evil the land of the two kings, Syria and Ephraim, would be forsaken; the sign was the child.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Peter said of David: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”.

God swore to David that of the fruit of his loins he would raise up Christ, and notice the words: according to the flesh. Not according to the spirit. Christ sits on David's throne as the fruit of David's loins in the flesh.

That is why the angel spoke to “Joseph, thou son of David”, and why “that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost” means it is of the prophecy: the promise sworn to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132 that the king would come out of his bowels, the fruit of his body.

So the child of Matthew 1 is the Christ God swore to raise up of the fruit of David's loins, according to the flesh, to sit on his throne. The bloodline is the birthright.

precepts.text: Strangers of Rome. We were the Romans too. Verse 5 already told you: Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven. We were called Romans, we were called Greeks, we were called barbarians.
precepts.point: Book read in class: Israel Redivivus, being a history of the tribes of Israel distinct from that of Judah, by Frederick Charles Danvers: with regard to the Israelites, it must be remembered that each tribe was divided into different families or subtribes, even as there were at a later date many tribes bearing different names who were collectively known to the Greeks as Scythians. The Scythians were nomadic people of that area. We were scattered everywhere, so we are the Barbarians, we are the Scythians, we are the Greeks. This is our book.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Barbarian was the word the Greeks used for all foreigners, including the Romans. And we were the Romans too; that is what mainstream Christianity does not understand today. Acts 2 lists the people gathered at Pentecost: “Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes.”

Strangers of Rome. And verse 5 already said who they all were: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Jews, devout men, out of every nation.

So we were called Romans, we were called Greeks, we were called barbarians. When Colossians 3:11 says “neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian,” those are the names Israel carried in the places it was scattered, not the other nations.

precepts.text: There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, come together for the feast of Pentecost: devout Jews, devout like Cornelius, out of every nation. God is no respecter of persons; those that keep the commandments have a place of repentance.
precepts.point: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. That is what he came to understand: Israel, the ones that were called not God's people, would one day be joined back in.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Peter says, “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” Every nation: Acts 2 shows who was in every nation. “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

They had come together for the feast of Pentecost: “And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.” These were devout Jews, devout like Cornelius, gathered out of every nation where they had been scattered. So “every nation” in Peter’s words is not every race of people; it is the Israelites living in every nation under heaven.

And God received them. “Suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind”, “cloven tongues like as of fire” sat upon each of them, “And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

That is what Peter came to understand at Cornelius’ house. God is no respecter of persons, northern kingdom or southern kingdom. Those that keep the commandments have a place of repentance, and Israel, the ones that were called not God’s people, would one day be joined back in.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
On the day of Pentecost “suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting”, and “they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.” That Holy Ghost was the mighty wind that filled them.

Acts 4 shows the same thing again: “And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.” The place shook, the Holy Ghost filled them, and the result was boldness.

When the apostles spoke and the Holy Ghost filled them, they were bold in what they said, because they knew what they were saying was sent of God, and they could prove it from the scriptures. That is the spirit that came on them at Pentecost: not a show, but a boldness to speak the word of God, grounded in knowing it.

At Pentecost they “began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.” Other tongues means other languages. The psalm already said it: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.”

There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard. The devout men dwelling at Jerusalem came “out of every nation under heaven”, because according to Deuteronomy 28 we were going to be scattered into all nations. So God made sure the word reached every one of them in the tongue wherein they were born. In every language the scattered people of Israel had taken on, their voice was heard, and the gathering of the twelve tribes began.

precepts.text: Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place, that I might leave my people, for they be all adulterers: separate from the unbelievers and set up a righteous underground railroad for believers, selfless instead of selfish.
precepts.point: Not sell your last, but consolidate your excess, because this place is over and the tribulation is coming while you run up credit cards.

note.label: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.why:
Jeremiah cries, “Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.” As these times come to pass, we have to strive to be among each other and to separate ourselves from these other nations and from the unbelievers, because they will continue to come for us.

That lodging place is what the believers in Acts 2 had. “All that believed were together, and had all things common”, and they “sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need.” Nothing was lacking among them. They were on one accord, breaking bread from house to house, on one accord with their finances, making sure no one who was lacking was left in a constraint. “And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.”

What the Lord wants us to set up in these last days is a righteous underground railroad: looking out for the believers, the ones striving and getting themselves together. That means being selfless instead of selfish. It does not mean sell your last. It means that if you have excess, start consolidating, because this place is over.

Too many are still running up their credit cards and putting everything in debt, not realizing the tribulation that is coming. As the tribulation happens we have to align ourselves with what the Lord is telling us to do: come out from among the adulterers and treacherous men, and make a lodging place for the believers.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
The great multitude is “of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues”, and the Christian says, see, we are all included. But read Acts 2:5: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

Out of every nation under heaven, and they were Jews. So “all nations” in Revelation 7:9 does not mean every race; it means the Israelites scattered into every nation, gathered out of them.

That is the all nations of Revelation 7:9: Jews out of every nation under heaven, the same people as the sand of the sea that cannot be numbered, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.

That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” This answers the question of who the people of all nations, kindreds and tongues are. They were Jews, Israelites, and they came out of every nation under heaven.

That is exactly what Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4: the Lord would scatter Israel among the nations. So when scripture shows a people coming out of every nation, it is not speaking of the nations themselves. It is speaking of Israel, found in every nation because the Lord scattered them there.

So Acts 2:5 is the key for Revelation 7:9. Out of every nation does not mean every nation's people; it means the devout Israelites dwelling among every nation, the same scattered people Deuteronomy 4:27 speaks of, who are seeking the Lord from thence.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who is far off? Peter answers it on the day of Pentecost: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call.”

The promise is to those Peter spoke to, to their children, and to all that are afar off. The far off are the ones who were cast off, the strangers of the northern kingdom scattered away from the land and the covenant.

So when Paul says Christ “came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh”, it is the same promise Peter preached. Christ taught the woman at the well and he taught the Jews: the far off and the nigh, both brought near by his blood.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Peter said, “Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” In every nation, because Israel is in every nation. Luke shows it at Pentecost: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

Israel is scattered everywhere, to all four corners: that is the vessel knit at the four corners in Peter's vision. So “in every nation he that feareth him” is not every people on earth; it is the Israelites scattered in every nation who fear God and work righteousness, like Cornelius, a devout man who feared God with all his house and gave much alms.

And read the next verse; they always skip it. “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”. The word was sent to the children of Israel. Those accepted in every nation are the children of Israel in every nation.

precepts.point: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. note.label: Numbers 21: The Fiery Serpents and the Serpent of Brass

precepts.why:
Christ said “whosoever believeth in him should not perish”, and the whosoever is defined in Acts. “And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved. Ye men of Israel, hear these words; Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs, which God did by him in the midst of you, as ye yourselves also know.”

Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved, and the next words are, ye men of Israel, hear these words. The whosoever is spoken to Israel.

The serpent of brass was lifted up for the Israelites that were bitten, and the salvation spoken of in the Son of man lifted up is for Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Here are Peter's strangers: Jews, devout men, scattered out of every nation under heaven.

Read on to verse 9 and the regions they came from are named, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia, the same places Peter's letter was sent to. So the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia are Jews, and the peculiar people Peter calls them is the peculiar people the Lord chose above all the nations that are upon the earth.

That is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are.

precepts.why:
“Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia”. The Jews dwelling at Jerusalem out of every nation came from Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia, the very regions Peter names when he writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”.

Line the two up and it is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are: Jews, Israel, scattered among the nations. So when Peter calls his readers a chosen generation and a peculiar people, he is speaking to the same people Moses spoke to, chosen to be a peculiar people above all the nations that are upon the earth.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David is a mighty warrior, so it sounds strange to hear him plead, “save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.” Peter gives the answer. He speaks “of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.” Yet “being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”, David foretold Christ long before he came.

That proves David was a prophet. He was not only speaking of his own time; he was prophesying for us in these last days, which means David is on the earth today. His prayer is our prayer too: that the Most High will save us from the hand of those who persecute us and want to come against us.

That is why the psalm speaks of an enemy that would “tear my soul like a lion, rending it in pieces, while there is none to deliver.” Rending our souls in pieces is how the other nations try to take advantage of us: the coronavirus was set up to rend our souls in pieces, mass incarceration was set up to rend our souls in pieces, medical apartheid was set up to rend our souls in pieces.

precepts.text: David is not ascended into the heavens, but he himself says the Lord said unto my Lord, sit thou on my right hand; so let all the house of Israel know that God has made that same Jesus, whom they crucified, both Lord and Christ.
precepts.point: The Lord said unto my Lord, sit thou at my right hand until I make thine enemies thy footstool. The one sitting at the Father's right hand is Christ.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.” Peter tells who is speaking and who is sitting: “For David is not ascended into the heavens: but he saith himself, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, Until I make thy foes thy footstool.”

David is not the one at the right hand; he is not ascended into the heavens. He himself says the Lord said it unto his Lord. “Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ.”

The one sitting at the Father's right hand is Christ, that same Jesus whom they crucified, and all the house of Israel is to know it assuredly.

precepts.text: Peter shews that David spake of the resurrection of Christ, for David is dead and buried and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
Peter shews that David spake of the resurrection of Christ. “For David speaketh concerning him, I foresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved: Therefore did my heart rejoice, and my tongue was glad; moreover also my flesh shall rest in hope: Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.”

Then Peter tells them plainly that David was not speaking of himself: “let me freely speak unto you of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.” David is dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day. “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne; He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.”

That is the scripture his disciples believed when he was risen from the dead: “they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.” David had written of the resurrection, and Christ had said, “in three days I will raise it up.” Both came to pass.

precepts.text: There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews out of every nation under heaven, because every nation that ruled over Israel carried them off into exile.
precepts.point: "All nations" does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria (which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled), then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece, and Rome, then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

That is what “all nations” looks like. These were not gentiles; they were Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, because every nation that ruled over Israel carried them off into exile. So when Christ commanded that repentance be preached “among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem”, it began with Israelites gathered at Jerusalem from every land they had been scattered into.

precepts.text: They were all filled with the Holy Ghost and began to speak with other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance; one instance of that power coming to pass.
precepts.point: Christians misunderstand this power as merely speaking in tongues, but the Bible defines the power of the Holy Ghost by the signs that follow: casting out devils, speaking with new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. Peter was sought to heal by his shadow and Paul by his handkerchief.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

That is one instance of the power coming to pass, the promise of Acts 1:8 fulfilled. But tongues is only one of the signs. The power of the Holy Ghost is casting out devils, new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. With that power they were witnesses “both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.”

precepts.text: Count fifty days after the Sabbath and offer a new meat offering of two wave loaves, the first fruits unto the Most High, which is Pentecost.
precepts.point: Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover. It is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits, and Israel kept it through every captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, and Greek.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.” The disciples were keeping the feast, which confounds the claim that after Christ died the law was done away with. If the ceremonial law was nailed to the cross, why did the disciples keep gathering for Pentecost?

Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover: “ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete: Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days; and ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the Lord.”

“Ye shall bring out of your habitations two wave loaves”, “they are the firstfruits unto the Lord.” That is why it is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits. The law remained in effect after his death, and the disciples continued keeping the feast days written in Leviticus 23.

precepts.text: The verse the churches misuse to say do not judge us over holy days, when it is defending Israel's right to keep the Most High's feasts, not pagan customs.
precepts.point: Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover. It is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits, and Israel kept it through every captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, and Greek.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days.”

This is the verse the churches misuse to say, do not judge us over holy days. But it is defending Israel's right to keep the Most High's feasts, not pagan customs.

Christ never once said to stop keeping Passover, the feasts or the Sabbath. He was born around the feasts, killed through the Passover, went up at the feast of Tabernacles, and read in the synagogue every Sabbath, as his custom was. So the disciples were keeping Pentecost after his death, and no man was to judge them for it.

precepts.text: The one accord in one place: Peter, James, John, and the rest of the disciples all gathered together in the upper room.
precepts.point: Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover. It is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits, and Israel kept it through every captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, and Greek.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alpheus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.”

That is the one accord in one place. Peter, James, John and the rest of the disciples were all gathered together in the upper room, keeping the day of Pentecost after Christ had gone up.

precepts.text: Tobit kept the feast of Pentecost, the holy feast of the seven weeks, during the Assyrian captivity.
precepts.point: Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover. It is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits, and Israel kept it through every captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, and Greek.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Israel kept Pentecost through every captivity. Tobit, in the Assyrian captivity, says, “my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks.”

Pentecost is the holy feast of the seven weeks, the Feast of Weeks, and Israel was keeping it even in Assyria. The disciples were keeping the same feast in Acts 2.

precepts.text: Israel kept the feast of weeks, called Pentecost, in Jerusalem during the Greek captivity.
precepts.point: Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover. It is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits, and Israel kept it through every captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, and Greek.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“And so they came to Jerusalem, the feast of the weeks approaching. And after the feast, called Pentecost, they went forth against Gorgias the governor of Idumea.”

Israel kept the feast of weeks, called Pentecost, in Jerusalem during the Greek captivity. Through the Assyrian, the Babylonian and the Greek captivities, Israel kept Pentecost, and after Christ died the disciples kept it still: “when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.”

precepts.text: The whole earth was of one language and one speech, showing a tongue is a language and a dialect.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Cloven means split or divided, and tongues means dialects, languages and speech. Go back to Babel and the word defines itself: “And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.” A tongue is a language. It is not the unknown babble the Pentecostal and Baptist churches practice.

The front of the King James Bible itself says it was translated out of the original tongues, meaning Hebrew and Greek, different languages. That is what a tongue is in the scriptures.

The glossolalia established in the churches in the late 1800s and 1900s is a pagan spirit giving utterance, the spirit of Satan, not the Holy Ghost. You cannot learn or teach the knowledge of the Most High through babble that no one can interpret. What sat on the apostles was divided languages, real speech, so the word could be taught.

precepts.text: Day unto day uttereth speech, and there is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard; their line is gone out through all the earth to the end of the world.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
David uses the same words the way Genesis 11 does: “Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge. There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” Speech and language are the same thing as tongues, and speech carries knowledge. A tongue is something that can be heard and understood, not babble.

“Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.” The words go out to the end of the world in every speech and language. That is what the cloven tongues were: the word of the Most High going out in the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed.

precepts.text: Whom shall he teach knowledge? With stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people, precept upon precept, line upon line.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” Knowledge and doctrine are taught, and they are taught “precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. That is how the knowledge of the Most High is learned, one scripture proving another. It can never be learned through babble that no one can interpret.

Then: “For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.” Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, so the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue, the languages of the lands they were carried into.

That is the cloven tongues of Acts 2. The divided tongues were the many languages of the nations where Israel was dispersed, and in them the word of the Most High went to this people.

precepts.text: The Most High would bring a nation from far whose tongue thou shalt not understand, which is why Israel had to be taught in the captors' languages.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
The curse tells why other tongues were needed: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”. Israel would be put under nations whose language they did not know.

Scattered among those nations, Israel took on the speech of their captors, so they had to be taught in the captors' languages. The cloven tongues that sat on the apostles were those languages, divided out so the word of the Most High could reach his people wherever they had been carried.

precepts.text: The title on the cross was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin, the languages of the captivities Israel was placed under.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Pilate's title on the cross shows the tongues in Jerusalem itself: “JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS. This title then read many of the Jews”, and “it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin.”

Those are the languages of the captivities Israel was placed under, and many of the Jews read them. Israel had been placed under those captivities, which is why the word had to go to them in those languages. So when the cloven tongues sat on the apostles, they were divided into the languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, the very languages written over Christ's head.

precepts.text: Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire; when the tongues appeared like fire, they spoke the word of the Most High in the scattered nations' languages.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
The tongues appeared “like as of fire”, and Jeremiah shows what the fire is: “Because ye speak this word, behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.” The word of the Most High in a man's mouth is fire.

That is what came upon the apostles. The divided tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was scattered, and in those languages they spoke the word of the Most High like fire.

precepts.text: Ye shall receive power after the Holy Ghost is come upon you, and be witnesses unto the uttermost parts of the earth; speaking an unlearned language is that power.
precepts.point: They were filled with the wisdom of the Most High to interpret and speak in the different languages of the lands where Israel had been deported, not glossolalia. If Christ commanded them to go teach all nations, they had to be given the power to speak in the tongues of those nations, and these illiterate Galileans spoke perfectly in languages they never learned.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Christ had told them what was coming: “But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.” Speaking a language you never learned is that power.

They were filled with the wisdom of the Most High to interpret and speak in the different languages of the lands where Israel had been deported, not glossolalia. These were illiterate Galileans, and they spoke perfectly in languages they never learned, because they were sent to witness unto the uttermost part of the earth, where the people were.

precepts.text: Go into all the world and preach the gospel, and these signs shall follow: they shall speak with new tongues, because they were going into all the world.
precepts.point: They were filled with the wisdom of the Most High to interpret and speak in the different languages of the lands where Israel had been deported, not glossolalia. If Christ commanded them to go teach all nations, they had to be given the power to speak in the tongues of those nations, and these illiterate Galileans spoke perfectly in languages they never learned.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.” If Christ commanded them to go and teach all nations, they had to be given the power to speak in the tongues of those nations.

So among the signs that follow them that believe: “they shall speak with new tongues”. New tongues, because they were going into all the world. That is what filled with the Holy Ghost means here: illiterate Galileans given the wisdom to speak the languages of the lands where Israel had been deported, so the gospel could be preached there.

precepts.text: Paul was accused as a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, showing Israel was scattered worldwide.
precepts.point: The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro says the Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock, were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. Swarthy means dark and black, tawny means copper or brown, and olive is not "all colors," for a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man; Christ was black and brown.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Paul's accusers called him “a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world”. The Jews were throughout the world. Israel had been scattered into all the kingdoms of the earth, which is why devout men, men who kept the laws, were dwelling at Jerusalem out of every nation under heaven.

Only one race of people was prophesied to be dispersed to every country. That is the reason men from every nation were present at Pentecost.

precepts.text: The Most High shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen.
precepts.point: The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro says the Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock, were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. Swarthy means dark and black, tawny means copper or brown, and olive is not "all colors," for a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man; Christ was black and brown.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Moses told Israel beforehand: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” Israel would be led among the nations and left few in number among the heathen.

Those few among every nation are the devout men of Acts 2:5, dwelling at Jerusalem out of every nation under heaven. They were there because the scattering had already happened, exactly as it was prophesied.

precepts.text: Thou shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth, the source verse from which the word diaspora comes.
precepts.point: The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro says the Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock, were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. Swarthy means dark and black, tawny means copper or brown, and olive is not "all colors," for a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man; Christ was black and brown.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” This is the source verse of the word diaspora. The word itself originated in the Septuagint at Deuteronomy 28:25, and the dictionaries define diaspora as the dispersion of the Jewish people beyond Israel.

There is no African diaspora that exists apart from this. The so-called African diaspora is the Israelite diaspora, because only Israel was scattered to all the earth by biblical prophecy. That is why Jews out of every nation under heaven were dwelling at Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The Most High shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.
precepts.point: The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro says the Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock, were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. Swarthy means dark and black, tawny means copper or brown, and olive is not "all colors," for a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man; Christ was black and brown.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”. From one end of the earth to the other is every nation under heaven, and that is where the devout men at Jerusalem had come from.

The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro bears it out. The Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock and were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction they were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. This verse is that divine prediction.

Swarthy means dark and black, and tawny means copper or brown. Olive is not all colors; a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man. Christ was black and brown.

precepts.text: Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated; since Esau fathered Rome, Paul's letters went to the Israelites in Rome, not to Edom.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians. But the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says, “Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.”

Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates. He was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers. The strangers of Rome at Pentecost are those scattered Israelites in the Roman provinces, not the Romans themselves.

precepts.text: To all that be in Rome, beloved of the Most High, called to be saints, the scattered Israelites who had gone off into greco-roman customs.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Read who the letter is addressed to: “To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints”. Beloved of the Most High. Esau he hated, so the beloved in Rome are not Edom; they are the scattered Israelites who had gone off into greco-roman customs and were living in Rome as strangers.

A stranger is one who does not originally live in a land but was dispersed there. The strangers of Rome who heard the apostles at Pentecost are the same people Paul later wrote to.

precepts.text: Aquila a Jew born in Pontus, lately come from Italy because Claudius commanded all Jews to depart from Rome; Israelites were strangers in Rome.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Here is one of the strangers of Rome by name: “a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”. A Jew born in Pontus, one of the lands on the Pentecost map, who had been living in Italy until Claudius put all the Jews out of Rome.

Israelites were strangers in Rome. They lived there, worked there as tentmakers, and could be commanded to leave, because it was not originally their land; they had been dispersed there. That is what the strangers of Rome means.

precepts.text: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob, in the day that strangers carried away captive his forces, thou stoodest on the other side; the day Israel became a stranger.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Obadiah shows the day Israel became a stranger. To Edom: “For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.”

Strangers carried Jacob's forces away captive, and Esau stood on the other side, as one of the enemy. From that captivity Israel was dispersed into other men's lands, and so Israel became the stranger in them. The strangers of Rome are Jacob's children carried into Edom's own empire, and Edom is the brother who is to be cut off for ever.

precepts.text: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, elect according to the foreknowledge of the Most High.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Peter writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”. The same lands that are on the map in Acts 2, Pontus and Asia among them, and the same word: strangers, people scattered into lands not originally their own.

These strangers are the elect according to the foreknowledge of the Most High, and the elect is Israel. So the strangers of Rome, and the strangers throughout these provinces, are the dispersed Israelites the apostles were sent to.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have called thee by thy name; the strangers were the elect according to the foreknowledge.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Who is the elect Peter wrote to? “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.” Israel is the elect.

So the strangers scattered through Pontus, Asia and the rest, elect according to the foreknowledge, are Israel, and the strangers of Rome standing in Jerusalem at Pentecost are Israel too. They had been surnamed, called by other names in other men's lands, though they did not know him, and now they heard the wonderful works of God in their own tongues.

precepts.text: I am in the midst of Israel and none else; I will pour out my Spirit, and whosoever shall call on the name of the Most High in Zion and Jerusalem shall be delivered.
precepts.point: "Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved" is defined by its audience. It is not the universal whosoever the churches pull from John 3:16; the whosoever is the Israelites scattered in the different lands.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Peter says this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel, so go to Joel and read what comes right before the pouring out: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” The Most High is in the midst of Israel. Then: “I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy”. All flesh is the house of Israel, not all nations, and the very next thing Peter says in Acts 2 confirms it: ye men of Israel.

The sons and daughters prophesying means they are given the ability to read and interpret the scriptures. The wonders, the blood and fire and the sun turned into darkness, are the signs before the great and terrible day of the Lord.

Then the whosoever: “whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.” The whosoever is defined by its audience. Deliverance is in Zion and Jerusalem and in the remnant the Lord calls: the Israelites scattered in the different lands.

precepts.text: The verse used for a universal whosoever, but in Acts 2 the whosoever is answered by "ye men of Israel."
precepts.point: "Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved" is defined by its audience. It is not the universal whosoever the churches pull from John 3:16; the whosoever is the Israelites scattered in the different lands.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:

In Acts 2 Peter says whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved, and the very next verse answers who that is: ye men of Israel. Joel said the same, that the Most High is in the midst of Israel and deliverance is in Zion and Jerusalem. The whosoever is the Israelites scattered in the different lands, not all nations.

precepts.text: Paul's heart's desire and prayer for Israel is that they might be saved, because he was writing to the Israelites in the Roman provinces.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

The audience never changed. These are the same people who asked in Acts 1:6 whether the kingdom would be restored to Israel. Peter proves who Christ is by walking through the prophecies of the Old Testament, and today we walk through those same prophecies to prove who Israel is.

That refutes the claim that the Old Testament is done away with. Everything the apostles preached was precept upon precept out of the law and the prophets.

precepts.text: The Most High sware in truth unto David, of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne; Christ the son of David is that king.
precepts.point: David is dead and buried and his sepulchre is still with us, so he was speaking as a prophet, not of himself. note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

David is dead and buried and his sepulchre is still with us, so he was not speaking of himself; he was speaking as a prophet. Knowing the Most High had sworn that a king from his seed would sit on his throne, David saw before and spoke of the resurrection of Christ. Christ the son of David is that king.

precepts.text: Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ was not revealed by flesh and blood but by the Father; understanding of the Messiah must be given.
precepts.point: David himself did not ascend, but said the Most High told his Lord to sit at his right hand until his foes are made his footstool, another prophecy pointing to Christ.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

Christ told him how he knew: “flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Understanding has to be opened for a man to know that Christ is the Messiah. It is given by the Father, which is why not everyone grasped it.

That is the same Peter now standing up as a witness that this Jesus the Most High raised up and exalted to his right hand. He knows it because it was revealed to him.

precepts.point: The gift of the Holy Ghost that follows is understanding being opened. Baptism with the Holy Ghost is the spirit of wisdom and understanding, seen when Christ opened the disciples' understanding to grasp the scriptures concerning him.
